# Properties

<!-- Generated by `mise run catalog:generate` from examples/catalog/: edit the entries, not this file. -->

Blender properties are declared as class annotations whose value is a call, `count: IntProperty()`, on a class that
takes properties (a *Property host*: a `PropertyGroup`, an `Operator`, `AddonPreferences` and a few more). Python
expects an annotation to name a type, not to call a function, so a plain type checker reports the call and does not
know what `self.count` is. The add-on typechecker reads it as Blender does: `self.count` is an `int` (the property's
*Value type*), and `bpy.types.Scene.x = IntProperty()` gives every scene an `x` (a *Registered property*).

[All topics](README.md) · [Reading an entry](README.md#reading-an-entry) · [By safeguard](by-safeguard.md) · [Roadmap](roadmap.md)

[Declaring properties](#declaring) · [Value types](#value-types) · [Registered properties](#registered) · [Callbacks and wrappers](#callbacks)

<a id="declaring"></a>
## Declaring properties

<a id="annotated-property"></a>
### A property declared as an annotation

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/annotated-property`

A Property host declares its properties as class annotations, `name: IntProperty(...)`. The annotation is a call,
which the typing spec rejects, but the checker reads it as a declaration: the attribute has the property's Value
type on every instance.

```python
from bpy.props import IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    count: IntProperty(default=2, min=0)


def example(settings: Settings) -> None:
    assert_type(settings.count, int)
    settings.count = "two"  # reported: invalid-assignment
```

- **What you see:** `settings.count` is `int`; ty reports [`invalid-assignment`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-assignment) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/annotated_property.py)

<a id="future-annotations"></a>
### `from __future__ import annotations`

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/future-annotations`

With `from __future__ import annotations` every annotation is a string, which Blender evaluates when it registers
the class. A `PointerProperty` can then name a class defined further down the module. The checker evaluates the
string the same way.

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from bpy.props import FloatProperty, PointerProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


class Brush(PropertyGroup):
    falloff: PointerProperty(type=Falloff)


class Falloff(PropertyGroup):
    radius: FloatProperty(default=1.0)


def radius(brush: Brush) -> float:
    return brush.falloff.radius
```

- **What you see:** `brush.falloff` is `Falloff`.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/future_annotations.py)

<a id="keyword-arguments"></a>
### Property arguments are keyword-only

**Handled** by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/keyword-arguments`

Every argument of the `bpy.props` functions is keyword-only, so `StringProperty("Name")` raises `TypeError`. The
stubs say so, and any type checker reports it.

```python
from bpy.props import StringProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    name_ok: StringProperty(name="Name")
    name_wrong: StringProperty("Name")  # reported: too-many-positional-arguments
```

- **What you see:** ty reports [`too-many-positional-arguments`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#too-many-positional-arguments) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/keyword_arguments.py)

<a id="legacy-assignment"></a>
### The old `x = IntProperty()` form

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/legacy-assignment`

Before Blender 2.80 properties were class attributes, `count = IntProperty()`. Blender now ignores that form
without a word: the class registers, but has no such property. The checker reports the assignment, so it is not
mistaken for a declaration.

```python
from bpy.props import IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    count = IntProperty()  # reported: blender-legacy-property
    total: IntProperty()
```

- **What you see:** ty reports [`blender-legacy-property`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#blender-legacy-property) (warn) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/legacy_assignment.py)

<a id="mixin-annotations"></a>
### Properties declared on a mixin

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/mixin-annotations`

Annotations of a base class, and of a mixin that is no Blender class at all, become properties of every class that
derives from them. A subclass can replace one by declaring the name again.

```python
from bpy.props import FloatProperty, IntProperty, StringProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


class Labelled:
    label: StringProperty()


class Item(Labelled, PropertyGroup):
    weight: FloatProperty()


class Counted(Item):
    weight: IntProperty()


def example(item: Item, counted: Counted) -> None:
    assert_type(item.label, str)
    assert_type(item.weight, float)
    assert_type(counted.weight, int)
```

- **What you see:** `item.label` is `str`; `item.weight` is `float`; `counted.weight` is `int`.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/mixin_annotations.py)

<a id="property-hosts"></a>
### Classes that ignore property annotations

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/property-hosts`

Only some Blender classes are Property hosts: `PropertyGroup`, `Operator`, `Macro`, `AddonPreferences`, `UIList`,
`Node`, `NodeSocket`, `NodeTree`, `Gizmo` and a few more. A `Panel`, `Menu`, `Header` or `RenderEngine` registers with
its annotations silently dropped, so the checker reports a property declared on one.

```python
from bpy.props import BoolProperty
from bpy.types import Operator, Panel


class VIEW3D_PT_tools(Panel):
    bl_space_type = "VIEW_3D"
    bl_region_type = "UI"
    bl_label = "Tools"

    expanded: BoolProperty()  # reported: blender-unsupported-property-host


class OBJECT_OT_tidy(Operator):
    bl_idname = "object.tidy"
    bl_label = "Tidy"

    recursive: BoolProperty()
```

- **What you see:** ty reports [`blender-unsupported-property-host`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#blender-unsupported-property-host) (warn) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/property_hosts.py)

<a id="rejected-arguments"></a>
### Arguments Blender rejects at registration

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) and [Blender at runtime](by-safeguard.md#blender-runtime) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/rejected-arguments`

Some `bpy.props` arguments type-check against the stubs but make `register_class` raise `ValueError`: a default
that is not one of the enum's items, a `set` callback without `get`, a vector `size` above
32. The checker reports each where it is written.

```python
from bpy.props import EnumProperty, FloatVectorProperty, IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup

MODES = [("FAST", "Fast", ""), ("EXACT", "Exact", "")]


def set_level(self, value: int) -> None:
    pass


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    mode: EnumProperty(items=MODES, default="SLOW")  # reported: blender-invalid-property
    level: IntProperty(set=set_level)  # reported: blender-invalid-property
    weights: FloatVectorProperty(size=40)  # reported: blender-invalid-property
```

- **What you see:** ty reports [`blender-invalid-property`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#blender-invalid-property) (error) on the lines marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [runtime evidence](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/props_defaults/_expected/runtime.toml) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/rejected_arguments.py)

<a id="value-types"></a>
## Value types

<a id="collection-property"></a>
### Collection properties

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/collection-property`

A `CollectionProperty` holds a list of `PropertyGroup` instances that Blender owns: `add()` creates one and returns
it, and items are looked up by index or by their `name`.

```python
from bpy.props import CollectionProperty, StringProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup, bpy_prop_collection_idprop


class Tag(PropertyGroup):
    colour: StringProperty()


class Library(PropertyGroup):
    tags: CollectionProperty(type=Tag)


def example(library: Library) -> None:
    assert_type(library.tags, bpy_prop_collection_idprop[Tag])
    assert_type(library.tags.add(), Tag)
```

- **What you see:** `library.tags` is `bpy_prop_collection_idprop[Tag]`; `library.tags.add()` is `Tag`.
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs have no generic `bpy_prop_collection_idprop`, so the Value type cannot be written.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/collection_property.py)

<a id="dynamic-enum"></a>
### Enum properties with dynamic items

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/dynamic-enum`

When `items` is a function, Blender calls it each time it needs the list, so the identifiers are only known at
runtime. The value is a `str`. Blender may call the function with `context=None`, and the stubs say so: a callback
annotated with `Context` alone is reported where it is passed.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.props import EnumProperty
from bpy.types import Context, PropertyGroup


def camera_items(self, context: Context | None):
    return [(o.name, o.name, "") for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "CAMERA"]


def light_items(self, context: Context):
    return [(o.name, o.name, "") for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "LIGHT"]


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    camera: EnumProperty(items=camera_items)
    light: EnumProperty(items=light_items)  # reported: invalid-argument-type


def example(settings: Settings) -> None:
    assert_type(settings.camera, str)
```

- **What you see:** `settings.camera` is `str`; ty reports [`invalid-argument-type`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-argument-type) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/dynamic_enum.py)

<a id="enum-items-unpacked"></a>
### Enum items that unpack another tuple

**Not handled** (planned) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/enum-items-unpacked`

Static `items` give the property a `Literal` Value type. When the sequence unpacks another one, `(first, *OTHERS)`,
the checker no longer reads the identifiers and the value is a plain `str`.

```python
from bpy.props import EnumProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup

FORMATS = (("OBJ", "Wavefront", ""), ("STL", "STL", ""))


class ExportSettings(PropertyGroup):
    file_format: EnumProperty(items=(("SCENE", "Scene", ""), *FORMATS), default="SCENE")


def example(settings: ExportSettings) -> None:
    # not handled yet: the unpacked identifiers are not read
    assert_type(settings.file_format, Literal["SCENE", "OBJ", "STL"])
```

- **Today:** ty reports [`type-assertion-failure`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#type-assertion-failure) (error) on the line marked *not handled yet*.
- **Future:** Planned: Read `*NAME` inside static `items` through the constant, as items joined with `+` already are. (tracked: `later/enum-items-unpacked`)
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/enum_items_unpacked.py)

<a id="pointer-properties"></a>
### Pointers to a group and to a data-block

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/pointer-properties`

A `PointerProperty` to a `PropertyGroup` always holds an instance of it: Blender creates it with its owner, and it
cannot be replaced. A pointer to a data-block type (`Object`, `Material`, ...) is `None` until it is set.

```python
from bpy.props import FloatProperty, PointerProperty
from bpy.types import Object, PropertyGroup


class Margins(PropertyGroup):
    top: FloatProperty()


class Layout(PropertyGroup):
    margins: PointerProperty(type=Margins)
    target: PointerProperty(type=Object)


def example(layout: Layout) -> None:
    assert_type(layout.margins, Margins)
    assert_type(layout.target, Object | None)
```

- **What you see:** `layout.margins` is `Margins`; `layout.target` is `Object | None`.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/pointer_properties.py)

<a id="read-only-properties"></a>
### Read-only properties

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/read-only-properties`

A property declared with `options={"READ_ONLY"}` can be read but not assigned: Blender raises `AttributeError` on
a write. The checker reads the option, keeps the Value type for reading, and reports an assignment; it takes a
property with a `get` callback and no `set` as read-only too.

```python
from bpy.props import IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


def get_total(self: "Settings") -> int:
    return 3


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    fixed: IntProperty(options={"READ_ONLY"})
    total: IntProperty(get=get_total)


def example(settings: Settings) -> None:
    assert_type(settings.fixed, int)
    settings.fixed = 1  # reported: invalid-assignment
    settings.total = 1  # reported: invalid-assignment
```

- **What you see:** `settings.fixed` is `int`; ty reports [`invalid-assignment`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-assignment) (error) on the lines marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [runtime evidence](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/generated/props_scalar/_expected/runtime.toml) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/read_only_properties.py)

<a id="scalar-types"></a>
### Scalar Value types

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/scalar-types`

`IntProperty`, `FloatProperty`, `BoolProperty` and `StringProperty` give `int`, `float`, `bool` and `str`. A string
with `subtype="BYTE_STRING"` gives `bytes`. A write of another type is an error.

```python
from bpy.props import BoolProperty, FloatProperty, IntProperty, StringProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    count: IntProperty()
    ratio: FloatProperty()
    enabled: BoolProperty()
    label: StringProperty()
    raw: StringProperty(subtype="BYTE_STRING")


def example(settings: Settings) -> None:
    assert_type(settings.count, int)
    assert_type(settings.ratio, float)
    assert_type(settings.enabled, bool)
    assert_type(settings.label, str)
    assert_type(settings.raw, bytes)
    settings.ratio = 1  # an int is a float
    settings.count = 1.5  # reported: invalid-assignment
```

- **What you see:** `settings.count` is `int`; `settings.ratio` is `float`; `settings.enabled` is `bool`; `settings.label` is `str`; `settings.raw` is `bytes`; ty reports [`invalid-assignment`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-assignment) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/scalar_types.py)

<a id="static-enum"></a>
### Enum properties with static items

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/static-enum`

An `EnumProperty` with a literal `items` sequence gives a `Literal` of its identifiers, so a typo in a comparison or
a write is reported. With `options={"ENUM_FLAG"}` the value is a `set` of them.

```python
from bpy.props import EnumProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup

AXES = [("X", "X", ""), ("Y", "Y", ""), ("Z", "Z", "")]


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    axis: EnumProperty(items=AXES)
    locked: EnumProperty(items=AXES, options={"ENUM_FLAG"})


def example(settings: Settings) -> None:
    assert_type(settings.axis, Literal["X", "Y", "Z"])
    assert_type(settings.locked, set[Literal["X", "Y", "Z"]])
    settings.axis = "W"  # reported: invalid-assignment
```

- **What you see:** `settings.axis` is `Literal["X", "Y", "Z"]`; `settings.locked` is `set[Literal["X", "Y", "Z"]]`; ty reports [`invalid-assignment`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-assignment) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/static_enum.py)

<a id="vector-subtypes"></a>
### Vector properties and their subtype

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/vector-subtypes`

A `FloatVectorProperty` gives a `mathutils` type chosen by its `subtype` and `size`: `Color` for a colour of size
3, `Vector` for a translation or direction, `Euler` and `Quaternion` for rotations, `Matrix` for a `MATRIX` of size
(4, 4) or 16. Any other subtype or size gives an array of floats.

```python
from bpy.props import FloatVectorProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup, bpy_prop_array
from mathutils import Color, Euler, Matrix, Vector


class Transform(PropertyGroup):
    tint: FloatVectorProperty(subtype="COLOR", size=3)
    offset: FloatVectorProperty(subtype="TRANSLATION")
    rotation: FloatVectorProperty(subtype="EULER", size=3)
    space: FloatVectorProperty(subtype="MATRIX", size=(4, 4))
    weights: FloatVectorProperty(size=5)


def example(transform: Transform) -> None:
    assert_type(transform.tint, Color)
    assert_type(transform.offset, Vector)
    assert_type(transform.rotation, Euler)
    assert_type(transform.space, Matrix)
    assert_type(transform.weights, bpy_prop_array[float])
```

- **What you see:** `transform.tint` is `Color`; `transform.offset` is `Vector`; `transform.rotation` is `Euler`; `transform.space` is `Matrix`; `transform.weights` is `bpy_prop_array[float]`.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/vector_subtypes.py)

<a id="vector-writes"></a>
### Writing a vector property

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) and [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/vector-writes`

A vector property reads as a `mathutils` object or an array, but takes any sequence of the right element type: a
tuple or a list, of rows for a `Matrix`. The checker types an add-on's own vector properties so, and the stubs
type Blender's (`Object.location`, `Light.color`) the same way. An element of the wrong type is still reported.

```python
from bpy.props import FloatVectorProperty
from bpy.types import Object, PropertyGroup
from mathutils import Color, Vector


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    tint: FloatVectorProperty(subtype="COLOR")


def example(settings: Settings, ob: Object) -> None:
    settings.tint = (1.0, 0.5, 0.0)
    assert_type(settings.tint, Color)
    ob.location = (1, 2, 3)
    assert_type(ob.location, Vector)
    ob.location = ("1", 2, 3)  # reported: invalid-assignment
```

- **What you see:** `settings.tint` is `Color`; `ob.location` is `Vector`; ty reports [`invalid-assignment`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-assignment) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs type `Object.location` as `Vector` for writes too, so assigning a tuple is reported.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [runtime evidence](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/api_setters/_expected/runtime.toml) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/vector_writes.py)

<a id="registered"></a>
## Registered properties

<a id="class-attribute"></a>
### The class attribute of a declared property

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/class-attribute`

A declared property exists on instances only. Once the class is registered, `Settings.count` raises
`AttributeError`: registration has turned the annotation into an RNA property. The checker reports the read.

```python
from bpy.props import IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    count: IntProperty()


def default_count() -> int:
    return Settings.count  # reported: missing-attribute
```

- **What you see:** ty reports [`missing-attribute`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#missing-attribute) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/class_attribute.py)

<a id="group-id-data"></a>
### The data-block that owns a group

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/group-id-data`

Every `PropertyGroup` instance knows the data-block it is stored on, `id_data`. The stubs can only say `ID`; the
checker narrows it to the types the group is registered on, here `Object`.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.props import FloatProperty, PointerProperty
from bpy.types import Object, PropertyGroup


class Physics(PropertyGroup):
    mass: FloatProperty(default=1.0)


def register() -> None:
    bpy.utils.register_class(Physics)
    bpy.types.Object.physics = PointerProperty(type=Physics)


def owner_name(physics: Physics) -> str:
    return physics.id_data.name
```

- **What you see:** `physics.id_data` is `Object`.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/group_id_data.py)

<a id="on-demand-property"></a>
### A property registered outside `register()`

**Partial**: handled in part by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/on-demand-property`

An add-on can register a property later than `register()`, say in an `update` callback when an option is turned
on. The checker knows the property only where `hasattr` has found it, and reports a plain read elsewhere. It also
reports the assignment that registers the property, which is legal there, as `missing-attribute`: outside
`register()`, `Scene` has no such attribute yet.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.props import BoolProperty, IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup, Scene

bl_info = {
    "name": "Catalog: a property registered outside register()",
    "author": "Blender Extension Developer Suite",
    "version": (1, 0, 0),
    "blender": (4, 2, 0),
    "category": "Development",
}


def enable_counter(self, context):
    # not handled yet: the registration outside `register()` is reported
    bpy.types.Scene.on_demand_count = IntProperty()


class ON_DEMAND_PROPERTY_Settings(PropertyGroup):
    counting: BoolProperty(update=enable_counter)


def example(scene: Scene) -> None:
    if hasattr(scene, "on_demand_count"):
        assert_type(scene.on_demand_count, int)
    print(scene.on_demand_count)  # reported: missing-attribute


def register():
    bpy.utils.register_class(ON_DEMAND_PROPERTY_Settings)


def unregister():
    bpy.utils.unregister_class(ON_DEMAND_PROPERTY_Settings)
```

- **What you see:** `scene.on_demand_count` is `int`; ty reports [`missing-attribute`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#missing-attribute) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **Not yet:** The assignment that registers the property outside `register()` is reported as `missing-attribute`.
- **Today:** ty reports [`missing-attribute`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#missing-attribute) (error) on the line marked *not handled yet*.
- **Future:** Possible: Accept assigning a property to a Blender class anywhere in the add-on, while giving the attribute only after `hasattr`.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/on_demand_property.py)

<a id="registered-property"></a>
### A property assigned to a Blender class

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/registered-property`

`bpy.types.Scene.x = PointerProperty(...)` adds a Registered property to every scene. The checker reads the
assignment wherever the add-on (or here, the script) makes it, and gives the attribute its Value type; `del` removes it
again.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.props import IntProperty, PointerProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup, Scene


class RenderPasses(PropertyGroup):
    count: IntProperty(default=1)


def register() -> None:
    bpy.utils.register_class(RenderPasses)
    bpy.types.Scene.render_passes = PointerProperty(type=RenderPasses)


def unregister() -> None:
    del bpy.types.Scene.render_passes
    bpy.utils.unregister_class(RenderPasses)


def pass_count(scene: Scene) -> int:
    return scene.render_passes.count
```

- **What you see:** `scene.render_passes` is `RenderPasses`.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/registered_property.py)

<a id="unsupported-target"></a>
### Classes that take no Registered properties

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/unsupported-target`

Registered properties work on every data-block type and on bones, nodes, sockets, view layers and strips, but not
on `Area`, `Window`, `Modifier`, `Preferences`, `Context` or a `SpaceView3D`. The checker reports the assignment.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.props import BoolProperty


def register() -> None:
    bpy.types.Object.pinned = BoolProperty()
    bpy.types.Area.pinned = BoolProperty()  # reported: blender-unsupported-property-target
```

- **What you see:** ty reports [`blender-unsupported-property-target`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#blender-unsupported-property-target) (warn) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/unsupported_target.py)

<a id="callbacks"></a>
## Callbacks and wrappers

<a id="callback-self"></a>
### `self` in property callbacks

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/callback-self`

Blender calls a property's `update`, `get`, `set`, `poll` and `items` callbacks with the instance that holds the
property as `self`, though they are plain functions. The checker knows which class that is: a lambda's `self` is the
declaring class, and a function whose `self` is annotated with another class is reported where it is passed.

```python
from bpy.props import FloatProperty, StringProperty
from bpy.types import Context, Object, PropertyGroup


def clamp_ratio(self: "Settings", context: Context) -> None:
    if self.ratio > self.limit:
        self.ratio = self.limit


def rename_object(self: Object, context: Context) -> None:
    self.name = "Settings changed"


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    limit: FloatProperty(default=1.0)
    ratio: FloatProperty(update=clamp_ratio)
    label: StringProperty(get=lambda self: f"{assert_type(self, Settings).ratio:.0%}")
    other: FloatProperty(update=rename_object)  # reported: invalid-argument-type
```

- **What you see:** `self` is `Settings`; ty reports [`invalid-argument-type`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-argument-type) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/callback_self.py)

<a id="enum-item-strings"></a>
### Strings returned by dynamic enum items

**Not handled** (not statically checkable) · not machine-checked · `properties/enum-item-strings`

Blender does not copy the strings an `items` callback returns. When Python frees them, the enum shows garbage or
Blender crashes, so the callback has to keep its list alive, for example in a module-level variable. Whether it does
is a question of object lifetimes, which no static check can answer.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.props import EnumProperty
from bpy.types import Context, PropertyGroup

_items_cache = []


def material_items(self, context: Context | None):
    _items_cache[:] = [(m.name, m.name, "") for m in bpy.data.materials]
    return _items_cache


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    material: EnumProperty(items=material_items)
```

- **Future:** Not statically checkable: Whether Python still holds the strings depends on what the callback built and kept while Blender runs.
- **Not machine-checked:** the code is type-checked, so its API names exist, but nothing in it is asserted.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [bpy.props](https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.props.html) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/enum_item_strings.py)

<a id="min-above-max"></a>
### A minimum above the maximum

**Not handled** (possible) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/min-above-max`

Blender rejects many wrong `bpy.props` arguments at registration, but not a `min` above `max`: the class registers
and the property keeps both limits, so no value is in range. Nothing reports it yet.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.props import IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup

bl_info = {
    "name": "Catalog: a minimum above the maximum",
    "author": "Blender Extension Developer Suite",
    "version": (1, 0, 0),
    "blender": (4, 2, 0),
    "category": "Development",
}


class MIN_ABOVE_MAX_Settings(PropertyGroup):
    # not handled yet: the limits are not compared
    level: IntProperty(min=10, max=0)  # would be reported: blender-invalid-property


def register():
    bpy.utils.register_class(MIN_ABOVE_MAX_Settings)


def unregister():
    bpy.utils.unregister_class(MIN_ABOVE_MAX_Settings)
```

- **Today:** nothing is reported on the line marked *not handled yet*.
- **Future:** Possible: Compare literal `min` and `max` (and `soft_min` and `soft_max`) in `blender-invalid-property`.
- **Checked in Blender:** the add-on registers; Blender keeps the minimum as given.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/min_above_max.py)

<a id="property-wrappers"></a>
### Constants, `partial` and wrapper functions

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/property-wrappers`

Add-ons share declarations: a module constant, `functools.partial`, a small function that returns a property. The
checker evaluates the annotation as a value, so each gives the Value type of the call it stands for.

```python
from functools import partial

from bpy.props import FloatProperty, IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup

OPACITY = FloatProperty(min=0.0, max=1.0)
Percent = partial(IntProperty, min=0, max=100, subtype="PERCENTAGE")


def distance(name: str):
    return FloatProperty(name=name, subtype="DISTANCE")


class Style(PropertyGroup):
    opacity: OPACITY
    fill: Percent()
    margin: distance("Margin")


def example(style: Style) -> None:
    assert_type(style.opacity, float)
    assert_type(style.fill, int)
    assert_type(style.margin, float)
```

- **What you see:** `style.opacity` is `float`; `style.fill` is `int`; `style.margin` is `float`.
- **More:** [feature tests: property_wrappers](../../tests/typecheck/features/property_wrappers/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/property_wrappers.py)

<a id="quoted-wrapper-call"></a>
### A wrapper call in a quoted annotation

**Not handled** (possible) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/quoted-wrapper-call`

Blender evaluates a string annotation when it registers the class, so `size: "distance('Size')"` declares a
property like the unquoted call. The checker parses the string as a type expression instead, and does not read the
call.

```python
from bpy.props import FloatProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


def distance(name: str):
    return FloatProperty(name=name, subtype="DISTANCE")


class Shape(PropertyGroup):
    # not handled yet: reported as a call in a type expression
    size: "distance('Size')"


def example(shape: Shape) -> None:
    # not handled yet: the quoted call is not read as a declaration
    assert_type(shape.size, float)
```

- **Today:** ty reports [`invalid-type-form`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-type-form) (error) and [`type-assertion-failure`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#type-assertion-failure) (error) on the lines marked *not handled yet*.
- **Future:** Possible: Evaluate a string annotation that holds a call as the call, as Blender does when it registers the class.
- **More:** [feature tests: property_wrappers](../../tests/typecheck/features/property_wrappers/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/quoted_wrapper_call.py)

<a id="unevaluated-annotation"></a>
### An annotation the checker cannot evaluate

**Partial**: handled in part by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/unevaluated-annotation`

When the checker cannot tell what an annotation evaluates to (a declaration built in a loop and picked from a
dict), it does not report the annotation as an invalid type: the attribute is `Any`, so nothing on it is checked.

```python
from bpy.props import FloatProperty, IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup

KINDS = {}
for name, factory in (("count", IntProperty), ("ratio", FloatProperty)):
    KINDS[name] = factory()


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    count: KINDS["count"]


def example(settings: Settings) -> None:
    assert_type(settings.count, Any)
    # not handled yet: the Value type is not known
    assert_type(settings.count, int)
```

- **What you see:** `settings.count` is `Any`.
- **Not yet:** The attribute is `Any` instead of its Value type.
- **Today:** ty reports [`type-assertion-failure`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#type-assertion-failure) (error) on the line marked *not handled yet*.
- **Future:** Possible: Follow a declaration built in a loop or read from a registry, as far as its values are literals.
- **More:** [feature tests: property_wrappers](../../tests/typecheck/features/property_wrappers/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/unevaluated_annotation.py)
